visa_requirement_type: Visa-exempt for Bangladeshi citizens; visitor permit may be granted on arrival
maximum_permitted_stay: A visitor permit may be granted for up to six months; it may be extended so the total stay does not exceed 12 months from the date of entry. The immigration officer decides the period.
entry_count: No visa; visitor permit assessed at each arrival
passport_validity_rule: Valid passport with at least six months validity beyond the planned return date, per Montserrat Tourism Authority guidance.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No fixed blank-page count stated in the official sources reviewed.
return_ticket_rule: An immigration officer may request evidence of a return ticket or sufficient money to pay the return fare; no fixed ticket format is stated.
proof_of_funds_rule: An officer may request evidence of sufficient funds to maintain during the visit and provide the return fare; no minimum amount is published.
accommodation_rule: No universal hotel-booking requirement is stated in the sources reviewed; provide host or accommodation details if requested.
travel_insurance_rule: No general mandatory visitor travel-insurance requirement was identified in the cited official guidance.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: No Bangladesh-specific vaccination rule was identified in the cited entry guidance; check transit-country and current public-health requirements.
transit_rule: Bangladeshi citizens are visa-exempt for Montserrat. Immigration Act provisions also allow a visitor/transit permit; airside transit procedures are not separately specified.
application_channel: No advance visa application. Complete the online Immigration and Customs / ED form before arrival (available up to 72 hours before travel), present a valid passport, and seek admission; a visitor permit may be granted at the port by the immigration officer.
application_fee: No visa fee for Bangladeshi citizens; no visitor-permit fee identified in official sources.
processing_time: No visa processing; the visitor-permit decision is made at the port of entry.
required_documents: Valid ordinary Bangladesh passport with at least six months validity beyond planned return | Online Immigration and Customs / ED form completed before arrival | Return/onward ticket or funds for return if requested | Evidence of sufficient funds for the stay if requested | Evidence of employment elsewhere and intention to return if requested.
official_immigration_source_name: Government of Montserrat Immigration Department — Countries Not Requiring a Visa
cross_check_source_name: Government of Montserrat — Immigration Act and Subsidiary Legislation (2025 revision)
review_notes: The official Government of Montserrat immigration portal lists Bangladesh among countries not requiring a visa. The statutory Immigration (Visa Exemption) Order applies to citizens or belongers of Bangladesh holding a valid passport and is not restricted to diplomatic or official passports. Immigration Act section 22 allows a visitor permit for up to six months and extension to a total of 12 months from entry, at officer discretion. Tourism Authority guidance requires a passport valid six months beyond planned return and an online ED form before arrival. Immigration Regulations regulation 17(3) allows an officer to request evidence of employment elsewhere and intention to return, a return ticket or funds for return, and sufficient funds for maintenance. This is visa-exempt entry, not visa-on-arrival.
notes: No advance visa application. Complete the online ED form before arrival. A visitor permit may be granted at the border at officer discretion. Employment is not permitted without the appropriate work authorisation. An immigration officer may take a photograph or fingerprints if required under the Act; this is not a pre-travel visa-photo requirement.

visa_requirement_type: U.S. B-2 or combined B1/B2 visitor visa required; Bangladesh B1/B2 visa-bond condition applies
maximum_permitted_stay: The period of admission is determined by U.S. Customs and Border Protection at the port of entry and recorded on Form I-94. Visa validity is not the authorised length of stay.
entry_count: B1/B2: one entry; three-month visa validity under the Bangladesh reciprocity schedule. Check the actual visa annotation.
passport_validity_rule: Standard U.S. guidance requires a passport to be valid at least six months beyond the intended period of stay unless a country-specific agreement provides an exemption. Confirm the current CBP Six-Month Club rule before travel.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No universal blank-page count is stated in the general B-2 guidance; follow the issuing post's passport and visa-foil instructions.
return_ticket_rule: No universal return-ticket format is prescribed in the general B-2 guidance. Evidence of intent to depart may be requested; carry a credible onward/return itinerary.
proof_of_funds_rule: Applicants may be asked to show ability to pay all trip costs; no fixed minimum balance is published.
accommodation_rule: No universal hotel-booking requirement is stated in the general B-2 guidance; provide itinerary and lodging details where relevant.
travel_insurance_rule: No general mandatory travel-insurance requirement is stated in the cited B-2 guidance.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: No general B-2 visa vaccination requirement is stated in the cited visitor-visa guidance; separate public-health or itinerary requirements may apply.
transit_rule: For immediate and continuous transit through the United States, a C-1 transit visa may be required if the traveller does not hold a valid B visa or another applicable exception. A valid B1/B2 visa may be used for transit. The B1/B2 visa-bond condition applies to B1/B2 issuance, not to a C-1-only transit visa.
application_channel: Complete DS-160 online, pay the MRV fee and schedule an interview at the U.S. Embassy or Consulate responsible for the applicant's residence or nationality. Bangladesh-based applicants should follow current U.S. Embassy Dhaka instructions. If the consular officer directs a bond, complete DHS Form I-352 and pay only through the direct Pay.gov instructions supplied by the officer.
application_fee: US$185 MRV; no B1/B2 reciprocity fee. Visa bond is a separate refundable deposit if directed.
processing_time: Interview waits vary by post and availability; there is no guaranteed adjudication SLA. Administrative processing can add time.
required_documents: Valid ordinary Bangladesh passport | DS-160 confirmation page | MRV fee receipt | Digital photo uploaded with DS-160 (printed photo if upload fails or post requests) | Interview appointment | Evidence of trip purpose, intent to depart and ability to pay | If directed, DHS Form I-352 and visa bond payment through Pay.gov.
official_immigration_source_name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection — Entry requirements for non-U.S. citizens travelling to Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands
cross_check_source_name: U.S. Department of State — Visitor Visa (B-2)
review_notes: CBP states that entry requirements for non-U.S. citizens travelling to Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands are the same as entering the United States from any foreign destination; there is no separate Puerto Rico visa. The U.S. B-2/B1-B2 visitor visa route therefore applies to Bangladesh ordinary passport holders. Bangladesh is listed in the U.S. Department of State's 2 October 2026 Countries Subject to Visa Bonds notice, with implementation date 21 January 2026. Applicants otherwise eligible for a B1/B2 visa must post the bond amount directed by the consular officer: US$10,000, US$15,000 or US$20,000. The applicant must not pay before receiving the officer's direct instructions; use DHS Form I-352 and the supplied Pay.gov link. The bond is a refundable deposit subject to compliance, not a visa fee and not a guarantee of issuance. Bond holders must enter and exit through commercial-air ports of entry, including preclearance; charter air, general aviation, land and sea ports are not permitted. The Bangladesh reciprocity schedule lists B1/B2 as one entry and three months validity, with no reciprocity fee. The State Department fee schedule lists a US$185 MRV fee. The separate Visa Integrity Fee is enacted in 8 U.S.C. §1806, but the 22 July 2025 DHS Federal Register notice said it was not being implemented in that action and would be announced in a future publication; no later official collection notice was located in this check, and the State Department fee schedule still lists the US$185 MRV fee. Do not treat the integrity fee as currently payable unless official implementation instructions are issued.
notes: No separate Puerto Rico visa exists for this route; the U.S. B-2/B1-B2 visa and U.S. admission rules apply. Bangladesh B1/B2 applicants are subject to the U.S. visa-bond condition and commercial-air-only port restriction when a bond is posted. A cruise/sea port arrival is not permitted for a bond holder.

visa_requirement_type: U.S. B-2 or combined B1/B2 visitor visa required; Bangladesh B1/B2 visa-bond condition applies
maximum_permitted_stay: The period of admission is determined by U.S. Customs and Border Protection at the port of entry and recorded on Form I-94. Visa validity is not the authorised length of stay.
entry_count: B1/B2: one entry; three-month visa validity under the Bangladesh reciprocity schedule. Check the actual visa annotation.
passport_validity_rule: Standard U.S. guidance requires a passport to be valid at least six months beyond the intended period of stay unless a country-specific agreement provides an exemption. Confirm the current CBP Six-Month Club rule before travel.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No universal blank-page count is stated in the general B-2 guidance; follow the issuing post's passport and visa-foil instructions.
return_ticket_rule: No universal return-ticket format is prescribed in the general B-2 guidance. Evidence of intent to depart may be requested; carry a credible onward/return itinerary.
proof_of_funds_rule: Applicants may be asked to show ability to pay all trip costs; no fixed minimum balance is published.
accommodation_rule: No universal hotel-booking requirement is stated in the general B-2 guidance; provide itinerary and lodging details where relevant.
travel_insurance_rule: No general mandatory travel-insurance requirement is stated in the cited B-2 guidance.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: No general B-2 visa vaccination requirement is stated in the cited visitor-visa guidance; separate public-health or itinerary requirements may apply.
transit_rule: For immediate and continuous transit through the United States, a C-1 transit visa may be required if the traveller does not hold a valid B visa or another applicable exception. A valid B1/B2 visa may be used for transit. The B1/B2 visa-bond condition applies to B1/B2 issuance, not to a C-1-only transit visa.
application_channel: Complete DS-160 online, pay the MRV fee and schedule an interview at the U.S. Embassy or Consulate responsible for the applicant's residence or nationality. Bangladesh-based applicants should follow current U.S. Embassy Dhaka instructions. If the consular officer directs a bond, complete DHS Form I-352 and pay only through the direct Pay.gov instructions supplied by the officer.
application_fee: US$185 MRV; no B1/B2 reciprocity fee. Visa bond is a separate refundable deposit if directed.
processing_time: Interview waits vary by post and availability; there is no guaranteed adjudication SLA. Administrative processing can add time.
required_documents: Valid ordinary Bangladesh passport | DS-160 confirmation page | MRV fee receipt | Digital photo uploaded with DS-160 (printed photo if upload fails or post requests) | Interview appointment | Evidence of trip purpose, intent to depart and ability to pay | If directed, DHS Form I-352 and visa bond payment through Pay.gov.

review_notes: Bangladesh is listed in the U.S. Department of State's 2 October 2026 Countries Subject to Visa Bonds notice, with implementation date 21 January 2026. Applicants otherwise eligible for a B1/B2 visa must post the bond amount directed by the consular officer: US$10,000, US$15,000 or US$20,000. The applicant must not pay before receiving the officer's direct instructions; use DHS Form I-352 and the supplied Pay.gov link. The bond is a refundable deposit subject to compliance, not a visa fee and not a guarantee of issuance. Bond holders must enter and exit through commercial-air ports of entry, including preclearance; charter air, general aviation, land and sea ports are not permitted. The Bangladesh reciprocity schedule lists B1/B2 as one entry and three months validity, with no reciprocity fee. The State Department fee schedule lists a US$185 MRV fee. The separate Visa Integrity Fee is enacted in 8 U.S.C. §1806, but the 22 July 2025 DHS Federal Register notice said it was not being implemented in that action and would be announced in a future publication; no later official collection notice was located in this check, and the State Department fee schedule still lists the US$185 MRV fee. Do not treat the integrity fee as currently payable unless official implementation instructions are issued.
notes: Bangladesh ordinary passport holders need a U.S. visitor visa; Bangladesh is not on the Visa Waiver Program list. B1/B2 reciprocity is one entry and three months validity. The Bangladesh visa-bond programme applies to B1/B2 issuance: US$10,000/15,000/20,000 as directed at interview, paid only after official instructions. Bond holders must enter and exit through commercial air ports; sea/cruise, land, charter and general-aviation entry are not permitted. The visa bond is separate from the US$185 MRV fee. The statutory Visa Integrity Fee has not been confirmed as collectible by a later official notice in this check.
